labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is right: the printed 'iff' is false, and the true direction is GX.isSLSCInCC_univ_of_semilocallySimplyConnected in GX.Branched.Galois (DEC-27). STATEMENT REFUTED IS THE PAPER'S. RamcovGX.tex:1455-1457 says 'X is slsc iff X is slsc in itself', under the standing hypotheses of def:semi_locally_simple_connectedness (l.1451): X Hausdorff, connected, locally path-connected. 'Slsc in itself' is l.1451 with U = X and 'almost trivial' read literally (DEC-55, def:almost_trivial_loop l.1210). That is GX.IsSLSCInCC univ: Dense univ, and at every x an open, preconnected V ∋ x such that every loop of Ω(x,x,V) has its connected component in the compact-open Ω(x,x,X) meeting Ω(x,x,W) for every neighbourhood W of x (printed by #print in the probe). 'Slsc' is the usual notion of l.1156, read by DEC-41 as: some U ∈ 𝓝 x whose loops at x are null-homotopic in X (Path.Homotopic, rel endpoints). That is GX.SemilocallySimplyConnected. The refuted direction is 'slsc in itself ⇒ slsc', the same one the archipelago refutes. not_semilocallySimplyConnected_of_isSLSCInCC_univ_compact is ¬ ∀ X : Type, [T2Space] [ConnectedSpace] [LocPathConnectedSpace] [CompactSpace], IsSLSCInCC univ → SemilocallySimplyConnected X. That is the archipelago's ¬∀ with the extra [CompactSpace X] inside the negation, so it is strictly stronger than the refutation of the printed statement. Nothing narrower is hidden. WITNESS CHECKED. grifHEA is the circles of radius 1/(n+1) centred at 1/(n+1), all through 0, and grifHEB is its mirror image. grifConeA and grifConeB are the straight cones with apexes (±1/2, 1) in ℂ × ℝ, and eq_zero_of_mem_grifConeA_of_mem_grifConeB shows they meet only at 0. This is Griffiths' twin cone. The topology is the subspace topology of ℂ × ℝ: the probe checks `inferInstance = TopologicalSpace.induced Subtype.val _` by rfl, and MetrizableSpace and ConnectedSpace are inferred. CompactSpace comes from isCompact_grifSet, the image of compact sets. PathConnectedSpace is proved through the parametrisations of the two squares. LocPathConnectedSpace is genuine: the sum of two convex squares is locally path-connected, maps onto the space by a continuous closed surjection, and IsQuotientMap.locPathConnectedSpace (mathlib) applies. The topology is not trivialised. SLSC IN ITSELF IS CORRECT. Off 0, V is the path component of x in X ∖ cone B (or X ∖ cone A), which lies in a cone star-shaped about its apex, so its loops are null-homotopic (ContractibleSpace). At 0, V = {height < 1}. F₁ is the straight homotopy down the cone lines (grifR, grif_segment_mem). F₂ = grifColl contracts each circle of index < N through its own cone; it is (q,0) at τ = 0 and (0,0) at τ = 1, and it fixes the other circles. The result lies in the 2/N ball. Composed, they give the homotopy form IsSLSCIn univ, and IsSLSCIn.isSLSCInCC (strict) gives the literal one. NON-NULL-HOMOTOPY IS CORRECT; this is the heart. grifOmegaK runs a_{N+n} on [n, n+1/2] and b_{N+n} on [n+1/2, n+1] of s = t/(1-t), so it is ∏_{n≥N} a_n b_n, inside the 2/N ball. grifZ(δ)_{ij} is the winding of t ↦ χ_{b_j}(δ t)^{level of the exp-lift of χ_{a_i}∘δ}. grifZ_homotopic is stated for mathlib's Path.Homotopic, rel endpoints, and is proved by liftHomotopy of χ_{a_i}∘F, endpoint control, and cWinding_homotopic. grifZ_trans is the crossed-homomorphism law Z(δ₁δ₂) = Z(δ₁) + Z(δ₂) + x(δ₁)y(δ₂)ᵀ. grifFR is AddSubgroup.closure of the rank-one integer matrices u⊗v, i.e. the finite-rank matrices, so grifTheta is a genuine homomorphism into (ℕ→ℕ→ℤ)/FR (grifTheta_trans). It is homotopy-invariant, vanishes on loops of either earring (grifZ itself vanishes there: grifZ_of_HEA, grifZ_of_HEB), and grifZ_omega gives Z = [i ≤ j] on [N,∞)². grif_not_mem_FR is sound: an (r+1)×(r+1) unitriangular block has determinant 1, hence rank r+1 > r. The extension to the whole space goes in two gluings of the strict GX.VanKampen.Data, through grifMkData; the tethers come from path-connectedness. The FIRST gluing is on Y1 = X ∖ {P_B}. U1 = {height < 1} (path-connected) and V1 = cone A ∖ K, apex included (path-connected), with U1 ∩ V1 = cone A at heights in ]0,1[ (path-connected), and grif_cover1 shows they cover Y1. f = θ∘R on U1, trivial on U1 ∩ V1 because R maps it into the right earring. The SECOND gluing is on X. U2 = X ∖ {P_B} and V2 = cone B ∖ K, with U2 ∩ V2 = cone B at heights in ]0,1[, all three path-connected, and grif_cover2 shows they cover X. f = grifD1.Φ conjugated by a tether q_A ⇝ q_B. Agreement uses grifRP_conj and grifTheta_conj; the quotient is abelian. Φ_trans (D.Φ(γ·γ') = D.Φ γ · D.Φ γ') is general, for any Y, G and Data, and correct: the 2N-fine subdivision of γ·γ' is the two N-fine ones, the ψ factors are matched by ψ_congr, and the kernel checks it. In the final chain, a null-homotopy of ω is conjugated by c2 to give L ≃ refl at q_B. Then D2.Φ L = D2.Φ refl = 1, while D2.Φ L = grifF2 L = D1.Φ(C1·L·C1⁻¹) = θ(R(…)) = θ(ω) ≠ 1. Every link is a theorem. FINDING TRUE: the printed 'iff' fails among compact metrizable spaces (Peano continua). The unformalized remark ('slsc ⇔ slsc in itself ∧ homotopically Hausdorff') is correct in the homotopy reading, as the REPORT scopes it; one sentence of it is unscoped (minor finding 1). REPORT nit: not_semilocallySimplyConnected_of_isSLSCInCC_univ_compact is also not grif-prefixed, contrary to the notes. All names nevertheless contain grif/griffiths or are the two principals, and none contains 'Scaffold'.

findings.what: The first sentence, 'a counterexample to the converse cannot be homotopically Hausdorff at the bad point', is unscoped. The argument after it ('every loop of V is homotopic into every neighbourhood') is the homotopy form GX.AlmostTrivial, not DEC-55's literal reading, which is the paper's notion. In the literal reading the loop's connected component in the compact-open Ω(x,x,X) meets every Ω(x,x,W), and connected components need not be path components (homotopy classes). So from the literal 'slsc in itself' plus homotopically Hausdorff, slsc does not follow by this argument. The closing sentence of the remark is correctly scoped ('in the homotopy reading'), and the mathematics is right in that reading (checked: slsc-in-itself at x plus ⋂_W im π₁(W,x) = 1 gives slsc at x, and slsc gives homotopically Hausdorff). The remark is offered to the author, so its scope should be stated where it starts.
findings.fix: Begin the remark with 'In the homotopy reading of almost-trivial (GX.AlmostTrivial, GX.IsSLSCIn): …', or add that under DEC-55's literal form the corrected statement would also need the components of Ω(x,x,X) to be path components.
